text:
A or B at Lake Kawaguchi: rent a bike for ¥2,200 and ride to the bridge, or buy a ¥1,500 bus pass and reach the north shore in 27 minutes? Here's what each really gives you 👇

🗺️ Before you scroll on: the route and the map are here 👉 https://japanbystation.com/lake-kawaguchi-half-day-cycling

🅰️ THE BIKE

🚲 Q-BIKE is Fujikyu Railway's own bike share. In the app it's ¥1,100 per hour, never more than ¥3,300 a day. You need a credit card and a phone that can receive SMS.

🎫 No card? The ¥4,400 day pass is sold at the station baggage storage from 10:00, and the bike goes back by 17:00.

🌬️ The freedom is the point: stop anywhere on the shore. Fun Japan suggests an electric-assist bike if hills or distance worry you.

📍 Return it in the Kawaguchiko area. Q-BIKE charges for a bike left elsewhere until it's collected.

🅱️ THE BUS

🚌 The Red Line leaves the station every 15 minutes from 9:00 and runs around the east and north shores.

🗻 19 minutes to the Music and Forest Museum stop, 27 to Oishi Park. The tourism association says the brick promenade near the museums keeps Fuji in view the whole way.

⏰ Buses back run every 15 minutes, so a train deadline is easy to meet.

✅ OUR TAKE

Clear, calm day and a 16:48 train? We'd take the bike. Wind, rain or a 14:58 train? The bus, and walk the promenade.
